header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Aurora Labs), Samir Rao (Aurora Labs), Laila Brooks (Aurora Labs), Tom Yates (Aurora Labs - Security)
summary: Redwood Optimize demo focused on INT8 vs FP8 quality/latency tradeoffs and explicit rollback paths for worst-case fidelity drops. Agreed to run targeted worst-case prompt set, share cost delta, and onboard Aurora to the Optimize sandbox for a two-week canary. Security questions flagged around KMS and audit trails; Redwood to share SOC2 docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through the Optimize console decision path for precision profiles — INT8 versus FP8 — and show how rollback/fallback behaves in worst-case fidelity drops. Uh, Diego will demo the sandbox first.
[00:22] Diego: Great, yeah hi all. I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick agenda: 1) show baseline latency/cost on Aurora's sample workload, 2) show INT8 profile with fallback to FP8 for flagged prompts, 3) show decision rules + canary rollout, and 4) Q&A / next steps.
[00:45] Nina: Sounds good. For context, our prod tail latency 95p is around 420ms and we have a hard SLO at 500ms. We care about hallucination regressions for clinical text — even rare cases are unacceptable.
[01:10] Samir: also, we run on hybrid infra, we have private cluster and some burst to cloud, wanna know how routing works.
[01:30] Diego: yep, we'll cover smart routing. Ok screen is up — apologies if transcription of console labels is messy, sometimes, uh the OCR in these exports trips on widget names.
[02:05] Diego: Here's the baseline: FP16-like baseline at Aurora's sample qps gives avg 280ms token latency, cost X. When we flip to INT8 profile you see median drops to ~230ms and token cost goes down by approx 28% in this sample.
[02:40] Laila: When you say flip, is that model-level or route-level config? We need per-endpoint control to keep our sensitive endpoints on more conservative profiles.
[02:55] Diego: Route-level — you can pin per-route. We also support context-based rules: if prompt matches a flagged pattern it can override to FP8 or full-precision.
[03:18] Tom: On security, if we do fallbacks, are logs showing original token stream? We need audit logs not to leak PII and to be KMS-backed.
[03:35] Maya: Good call — we have audit trails and KMS integration. We'll share SOC2 and KMS docs after. The logs can be redacted per route, and RBAC can limit who sees raw transcripts.
[04:02] Diego: Ok, moving to worst-case scenarios — we uploaded Aurora's worst-case prompt set (30 prompts flagged from your QA). Showing the sensitivity heatmap: some prompts have large fidelity drops with INT8 — like prompt 7 and 21.
[04:25] Nina: Are these hallucinations or omissions? We need to classify what counts as regression.
[04:38] Diego: Mostly hallucinations; a few are subtle factual shifts. The console lets you tag severity and set trigger thresholds — e.g., if BLEU-like or custom eval metric drops by > 6% then automatically route that prompt to a safer precision.
[05:05] Maya: Important note — the rollback flow is deterministic: on a flagged failure we either 1) re-run the prompt on FP8 and compare, or 2) fall back to FP8 for N tokens then continue. You can pick re-run vs inline fallback.
[05:35] Samir: Re-run adds extra cost and latency, right?
[05:40] Diego: Correct — re-run is higher tail latency but gives stronger fidelity guarantees. Inline fallback reduces immediate latency hit by just switching execution path but might not catch all edge regressions.
[06:05] Laila: How do we set the canary? We want to test INT8 for 5% of traffic, but only for non-sensitive routes.
[06:20] Diego: In the rollout UI you pick route filters, percentage, and a quality gate. We support automatic rollback when regression is detected above your threshold. You can also schedule manual review for flagged cases.
[06:45] Nina: What's the false-positive rate of automatic flags? We can't have automated rollbacks that break availability.
[06:55] Maya: That's where the decision path helps — you can require two triggers or a human-in-the-loop threshold. The system sends alerts to your SRE and holds rollback pending approval if you choose.
[07:18] Tom: For audit, can we see the exact inputs that triggered a rollback? Needs to be retained for compliance but access controlled.
[07:35] Diego: Yes, full event detail is stored, retention configurable. We can also redact content at ingestion if you need that.
[08:00] Nina: On performance, I'm concerned about tail. If we put heavy fallback re-runs into the same pool it'll blow our 95p. Can Redwood isolate fallback reruns to a separate pool?
[08:15] Diego: Absolutely. We recommend a dedicated fallback pool or a lower-priority burst pool. That separates capacity and avoids impacting normal traffic.
[08:40] Samir: How does autoscaling interact? If fallbacks spike, will it auto-scale and cost skyrocket?
[08:50] Maya: You can set autoscale limits and budget caps. Also Optimize recommends batch profiles that reduce token costs in normal traffic so you get headroom for fallbacks.
[09:12] Diego: demoing the console's heatmap again — see prompt 21? It's a high-sensitivity signature. We can attach a per-prompt override: force FP8 for that prompt hash.
[09:35] Nina: Can we upload counterfactuals — like slightly modified prompts — to test sensitivity?
[09:45] Diego: Yes, you can upload a test corpus and run sweeps. We do an automated delta matrix: latency vs metric drop across quant levels.
[10:10] Laila: What about FP8 variability between providers and chipsets? Our private infra uses A100s, but cloud bursts may hit H100s.
[10:25] Diego: Right, FP8 execution differs across kernels. The runtime has kernel-selection profiles. Optimize includes a compatibility matrix per hardware and will recommend conservative profile when crossing hardware fleets.
[10:55] Samir: Any known gotchas for seq-lengths? Our prompts vary widely.
[11:05] Diego: Short seqs benefit less from quantization but long seqs show larger cost wins. Also KV-cache behavior matters; reusing caches reduces regression risk.
[11:40] Maya: quick demo of a decision rule: if metric delta >5% and route is tagged clinical then immediate rollback to FP8 and create ticket in JIRA. Otherwise hold and surface to ops.
[12:05] Tom: We need to check data residency — if the fallback re-run goes to cloud, does the data leave our VPC?
[12:20] Diego: No — you can pin sensitive routes to private stacks; the routing policy prevents sending those to hosted endpoints.
[12:40] Nina: Could you show a live A/B for prompt 7? I'd like to see exact outputs side-by-side.
[12:55] Diego: Sure — running pair now. Note: sometimes the side-by-side viewer truncates and may mislabel token offsets, the transcripts here might show slightly different punctuation.
[13:30] Diego: FP8 output (left) vs INT8 output (right) — you can see INT8 produced an extra assertion about procedure that looks like a hallucination.
[13:55] Laila: Hmm that's concerning. How often did that happen in your sweep?
[14:05] Diego: It was 3 out of 30 in the flagged set. But overall, INT8 had a 1.7% weighted metric drop across the whole eval.
[14:25] Nina: Weighted by what metric?
[14:30] Diego: By our custom clinical fidelity score — combination of entity preservation and hallucination penalty that your team provided.
[14:50] Samir: If we detect repeated hallucinations, can the system escalate to a model variant — like up-versioning to a different base model?
[14:58] Maya: Yes if you have multiple model variants available you can set fallback to another variant instead of only precision change. That is supported in the routing policy.
[15:20] Laila: Cost question: INT8 + occasional re-runs vs just FP8 baseline — how do we project cost over our 10M tokens/mo?
[15:30] Maya: We'll run the cost projection and send a delta. In general INT8 plus 5% re-runs often still saves compared to full FP8, but depends on false-positive rate.
[15:55] Diego: demo of automated alerting: when a profile breach happens an event is emitted to webhook and can create an incident in PagerDuty.
[16:10] Tom: For compliance we need SAML SSO and SCIM. Do you support SCIM user provisioning for the sandbox org?
[16:22] Maya: Yes, we have SSO + SCIM support; we'll share setup guide.
[16:40] Nina: On the worst-case prompt set, can we label certain prompts as 'never quantize' — e.g., consent forms and critical templates?
[16:55] Diego: yes — per-prompt or per-template pinning is supported. You can also tag a route as 'no quant' to prevent any precision change.
[17:20] Laila: Show me the rollback timing: how long from detection to re-run? Example numbers.
[17:30] Diego: Detection runs async — typically under 120ms to flag, then re-run depends on queue, but if you use dedicated fallback pool you can target sub-200ms extra, otherwise it could be 500-800ms.
[18:05] Samir: That variance is big. For clinical endpoints we can't accept >300ms additional.
[18:14] Maya: Then dedicate a fallback pool and set the re-run to a high-priority lane; we'll help size it.
[18:35] Nina: Is there historical traceability so we can see how a specific user's request routed over time?
[18:45] Diego: Yes, trace logs show route, precision used, fallback events, and the metric deltas; retained per your retention policy.
[19:05] Laila: Ok re: rollout plan — we want a small pilot: INT8 for 3% of traffic on non-clinical, 1 week, review daily.
[19:20] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll set up the canary, enable daily digest, and threshold alerts.
[19:40] Diego: Quick note on model calibration — we offer calibration sweeps that optimize quantization scales using your eval set; this reduces hallucinations.
[19:58] Nina: How invasive is calibration? Does it change model weights?
[20:05] Diego: No weight changes. It's numeric scaling and kernel tuning — non-destructive.
[20:22] Samir: Any dependence on tokenizer changes? Our tokenizer is custom.
[20:30] Diego: Tokenization differences get normalized; we advise running calibration with your tokenizer for best results.
[20:50] Maya: real-world anecdote: one customer saw 24% cost savings with INT8 and a set of per-prompt pins; they used re-run for 0.8% of traffic only.
[21:10] Laila: Ok. Can we see the raw CSV of the sweep? We want to feed it into our analysis pipeline.
[21:18] Diego: Yes, exports available. I'll attach the CSV to the follow-up email.
[21:35] Nina: Also need the SOC2 link and KMS integration docs.
[21:42] Maya: We'll include those in the email and the sandbox invite.
[22:00] Diego: Demoing the API call for on-demand re-run and the SDK quickstart. Note: SDK names sometimes are munged in transcriptions, so watch the actual repo link I'll share.
[22:25] Samir: Regarding private deployment: if we host Redwood Private on our VPC, can we still get Optimize recommendations from Redwood's console?
[22:40] Diego: Yes, Optimize can run in a hybrid mode — you push metrics and we provide profile suggestions, or run fully in your environment if desired.
[22:58] Tom: Any minimum commit for Dedicated pools here?
[23:05] Maya: For dedicated reserved capacity there are tiered contracts — we'll send options; for pilots we can do short-term reserved burst capacity.
[23:25] Laila: I want to call out an edge: composite prompts that call tools — do fallbacks handle tool-calls correctly?
[23:40] Diego: Tool-calls are treated like sequences; we have safe-handles to preserve tool output fidelity and can route tool-heavy prompts to FP8 by rule.
[24:05] Nina: Let's talk guarantees: if a rollback happens, can we tie that to SLA credits?
[24:18] Maya: Rollbacks are operational events; SLA credits for service outages are separate. For fidelity regressions we offer custom SLA language in enterprise contracts.
[24:40] Samir: Do you have benchmark numbers on re-run throughput? We need to size our fallback pool.
[24:50] Diego: I'll produce a sizing guide based on your qps and expected fallback rate; action item for me.
[25:10] Maya: Quick poll — who wants the sandbox invite now? (Laila, Nina raise hand)
[25:20] Maya: Ok we'll invite you, and Diego will seed the sandbox with your worst-case set.
[25:35] Diego: Jumping to the decision-path DSL briefly: rules are JSON-like, you can version them and roll them like configs.
[25:55] Laila: Nice, versioning is helpful for audits.
[26:10] Nina: Any examples of rollback causing regressions? i.e., rerunning produced worse output.
[26:20] Diego: Rare but possible if the model is nondeterministic; we include deterministic seeds to reduce that. Also you can prefer inline fallback vs re-run to avoid double-evaluation.
[26:50] Tom: For compliance again, who at Redwood has access to raw prompts? Need strict access controls.
[27:00] Maya: Access is limited, logged, and contractual. We'll provide a data access matrix.
[27:20] Samir: Is there a UI to replay a flagged request across different quant profiles? That'd be useful.
[27:28] Diego: Yes the sandbox has a replay tool to test multiple profiles side-by-side, exporting diffs.
[27:50] Laila: Ok show me the rollback audit view.
[27:58] Diego: opening audit view — shows event, trigger metric, action taken, ticket link — again console labels might be transcribed oddly but you'll get the link in the email.
[28:30] Nina: Anything else on risk mitigation for FP8? We're trying not to be surprised in prod.
[28:40] Diego: Multi-tier: pin critical routes, per-prompt pinning, fallback pools, conservative decision thresholds, daily digests, and manual approval gates.
[29:05] Maya: Proposed timeline — week 0: sandbox seeding + run initial sweep; week 1: small canary (3%); week 2: expand to 10% with monitoring; decide after week 3.
[29:25] Nina: That timeline works. We need the CSV and the pricing delta by Friday.
[29:35] Maya: We'll deliver both.
[29:50] Diego: Rapid demo end; flipping to Q&A — open floor.
[30:10] Laila: Does the Optimize tool recommend per-model thresholds or only per-route?
[30:18] Diego: Both — model-level defaults plus route overrides. And you can set global guardrails.
[30:40] Tom: For sandbox access, how long is the tenant active?
[30:50] Maya: We'll set it to 30 days by default, extendable.
[31:12] Nina: On the export, will the CSV include per-prompt token breakdowns?
[31:22] Diego: Yes, tokens, latency, metric deltas, and stack trace of which rule fired.
[31:40] Samir: Anything about model updates? If Redwood updates model weights, do precision profiles change behavior?
[31:50] Diego: Model updates can change sensitivity; we recommend re-running the calibration sweep after any model update and pin stable profiles for critical routes.
[32:10] Laila: Costs for calibration runs?
[32:18] Maya: Calibration is included for enterprise customers up to a degree; we'll outline optional paid lab runs in the follow-up.
[32:40] Diego: Ok final demo item: decision path logs can be exported to your SIEM via webhook.
[32:52] Tom: Great.
[33:05] Maya: Recap of agreed next steps: Diego runs the worst-case sweep on INT8+fallback, Maya sends pricing delta + SOC2 docs, Samir shares latency histograms, and Redwood sets up sandbox.
[33:25] Nina: Also want daily digest for canary.
[33:35] Maya: noted. Any last questions?
[33:45] Laila: No, thanks — this was helpful.
[34:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and invite. End meeting.

Note: Transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and OCR-like UI label errors; timestamps approximate.
